clue.text: Rebuke salesman with fish

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A boss tells off a salesman who turns up carrying fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproach is a scolding or expression of disapproval, so it is a synonym for a rebuke.

clue.text: Observe opening of estate agent

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: first letter of estate
a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: Someone watches the estate agent's office open for business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Estate agent' reads as one phrase, but the two words are split: one gives a letter, the other a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of something, a literary synonym for observe.

clue.text: Humiliated PM's predecessor kept in outhouse

indicators.note: something kept in a place is held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse
PM (afternoon) is preceded by AM (morning)

explanation.surface: A disgraced former Prime Minister is locked away in an outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like Prime Minister, but it is post meridiem; the time before it is AM, ante meridiem.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shamed has been publicly disgraced, the same as humiliated.

clue.text: Shorten Arsenal's first game

indicators.note: the first of a word is its initial letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of Arsenal
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A football report trimmed down to Arsenal's opening match of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club, which makes 'game' look like a football match; here it is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to cut it down to a shorter version, so it is a synonym for shorten.

clue.text: For example, good chess player that may be beaten by a whisker

definitions.text: that may be beaten by a whisker

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates 'for example'
G is the abbreviation for good
White is one of the two sides in chess

explanation.surface: A strong chess player who loses by the narrowest of margins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten by a whisker' suggests a narrow defeat, but a whisker here is a kitchen whisk, which beats the white of an egg into foam.
explanation.definitionFit: The white of an egg is what a cook whips into peaks with a whisk, so it is something a whisker beats.

clue.text: Remember Pooh's imaginary?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: keep something in your thoughts
second meaning, read literally: Winnie-the-Pooh is a bear, and an imaginary one exists only in someone's head

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading: Pooh is a toy bear, and if he is imaginary he lives in your mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning to keep a fact in mind and take it into account, so it equals remember.

clue.text: Stomachs revealed in parts of stadium

definitions.meaning: first meaning: puts up with, tolerates
second meaning: the tiered seating areas around a sports ground

explanation.surface: Bellies on show in the crowd at a football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomachs' looks like a plural noun for bellies, but it is a verb, meaning tolerates.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stands a thing tolerates it, as one who stomachs it does; a stadium's stands are its spectator sections.

clue.text: Emma's possibly greeting British lady in India

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters among many, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
hi is a greeting
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Emma, perhaps, greets an Englishwoman out in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Memsahib was the term of respect used in colonial India for a European married woman, so it names such a lady.

clue.text: Smashing jar, by the sound of it

indicators.note: judging by sound means the word is heard, not spelt, so a same-sounding word is wanted

parts.note: to grate is to jar, to have an irritating effect

explanation.surface: A jar breaking makes a smashing noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' and 'jar' together suggest breaking crockery, but smashing is British slang for excellent, and to jar is to grate.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is informal British praise meaning excellent or wonderful, which great also means.

clue.text: Attempt to cover front of aircraft carrier

indicators.note: to cover something is to go over and around it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of aircraft

explanation.surface: An attempt to protect the bow of an aircraft carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aircraft carrier' reads as a ship, but the phrase splits: aircraft gives a letter, and carrier alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray is a flat board for carrying dishes or drinks, so it is a carrier.

clue.text: Leading fighting, Home Guard leader

parts.note: main means chief or leading
war is fighting
in means at home

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: first letter of Guard

explanation.surface: A description of the officer leading the Home Guard into battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Mainwaring commands the Home Guard platoon in the BBC sitcom Dad's Army; the whole clue describes him while also building his name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dad's Army, the British wartime comedy, Captain Mainwaring is the pompous officer in charge of the local Home Guard unit.

clue.text: Cornered, but not beginning to be struck

indicators.note: without its beginning means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: cornered means trapped

explanation.surface: Someone backed into a corner but not yet hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapped means hit sharply, as on the knuckles, so it is a synonym for struck.

clue.text: Cricketer with top hat under pressure

indicators.note: in a down entry, what comes under another piece is written after it

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
ace means top, excellent
a bowler is a hard round hat

explanation.surface: A cricketer in a top hat finds himself under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top hat' reads as one item of headgear; the words split, with top giving ACE and hat giving a different hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pace bowler is a cricketer who bowls fast, as opposed to a spinner.

clue.text: Freedom of speech is blessing in disguise

indicators.note: something in disguise has its appearance changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Free speech is a hidden benefit, says the familiar phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freedom of speech' suggests the civil right, but here it means talking freely and too easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Glibness is a fluent, easy way of talking, a playful reading of speech that flows freely.

clue.text: Registration desk where visitors to Prague may be heard?

indicators.note: being heard means the phrase is spoken, so its sound counts, not its spelling

parts.note: Prague is the Czech capital, so visitors there are in the Czech lands

explanation.surface: A hotel reception desk in Prague welcoming tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: A check-in is the counter at a hotel or airport where arrivals register, so it is a registration desk.

clue.text: Being thrown out, I'd return as an uninvited guest

indicators.note: being thrown out of order suggests the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone ejected from a party vows to come back without an invitation.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder enters where they are not wanted, which is what an uninvited guest does.

clue.text: Sloe gin is bad for lots of soldiers

indicators.note: bad suggests something spoiled or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that sloe gin is no good for an army.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion is a large body of soldiers, so legions are lots of them.

clue.text: Leave brief message outside? Almost!

indicators.note: one piece sits outside the other, wrapping around it

parts.note: a note is a short message
to quit is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone about to leave scribbles a short note outside, and nearly gets it right.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not quite there means it is almost but not fully, so the phrase equals almost.

clue.text: Stepping out, missing last scrap

indicators.note: out suggests being out of place, so the letters are rearranged
missing its last means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stepping outside, someone realises the last bit of something is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the final G of stepping, then rearrange the seven letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece or fragment of something, which is what a scrap is.

clue.text: Teacher not about to waffle

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher who is not going to talk nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is British slang for talking at length about little, which is to waffle.

clue.text: Capital letter from Argos followed by one from Sparta

indicators.note: a single letter is taken from the word, here its first

parts.note: first letter of Argos
then means next, coming after

indicators.note: one letter is taken from the word, here its first

parts.note: first letter of Sparta

explanation.surface: A capital letter is sent from one ancient Greek city and answered from another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital letter' reads as an upper-case letter, but capital is the definition and the letters come from two Greek city names.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece, a country that also contains Argos and Sparta.

clue.text: Betting system involving American lawyer until now

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: the tote is a betting system pooling all stakes
a DA is a District Attorney in the US

explanation.surface: An American lawyer gets mixed up in a gambling scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To date is an idiom meaning so far, up to the present, which equals until now.

clue.text: Arrive with cycle at college

parts.note: a turn is one cycle or rotation
a student at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: A student arrives on a bike at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycle' suggests a bicycle, but it means one rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up is an idiom for appearing or arriving somewhere.

clue.text: Appear with top equestrian

parts.note: to show is to appear, as in turn up
a jumper is a sweater, a top worn on the upper body

explanation.surface: A rider appears alongside the best in the sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top equestrian' reads as a leading rider, but top is a garment: in Britain a jumper is a knitted sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A show jumper is a rider who competes at leaping fences on horseback, so is an equestrian.

clue.text: Individual music category

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the genre of Black American popular music

explanation.surface: A distinctive genre of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A soul is a single person, as in 'not a soul was there', and soul is also a style of rhythm-and-blues music.

clue.text: Something to attract shoppers in Jerusalem

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the following word

parts.note: letters three to six of the word

explanation.surface: A lure for shoppers in the markets of Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale offers reduced prices, a classic draw for shoppers.

clue.text: One of the family grannie certainly embraces

indicators.note: the words embrace the answer, holding it inside them across the gap

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Granny is sure to hug a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece, a sibling's daughter, is a relative and so one of the family.

clue.text: English attribute that makes no difference

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a quality is an attribute or characteristic

explanation.surface: A national characteristic of the English that changes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Equality is the state of being the same in value or status, with no difference between parties.
